This page is a list of official turning points, not a news feed.

Read the one-line note under each heading, then the dates.

“In force” means the instrument applies now. “Draft” or “guidance” means it does not yet bind operators by itself.

Hong Kong rules apply to this course. Mainland, United States, and EU rows are comparators.

## Hong Kong

These dates created Hong Kong’s working definition, the drone statute, two trial programmes, and the 1.4 GHz licence. The Action Plan text is still unpublished.

- 2022-12-01 — Cap. 448G. Hong Kong’s main drone statute took full effect. Students should treat later sandbox circulars as permissions under this Order, not as a replacement statute. [source](https://www.elegislation.gov.hk/hk/cap448G)
- 2024 (PA ¶82) — 2024 Policy Address ¶82. The government named low-altitude activity (generally below 1,000 m) as a policy field and created the Working Group. This is a policy announcement, not a new ordinance. [source](https://www.policyaddress.gov.hk/2024/en/p81.html)
- 2024-11-12 — Working Group first meeting. The cross-bureaux group began work. A first meeting is not the same thing as published implementing rules. [source](https://www.info.gov.hk/gia/general/202411/12/P2024111200260.htm)
- 2025-03-20 — Regulatory Sandbox 38 of 72. The first trial cohort was selected. These 38 projects are supervised tests, not an open commercial market, and must not be added to Sandbox X counts. [source](https://www.info.gov.hk/gia/general/202503/20/P2025032000179.htm)
- 2025-07-18 — Cap. 448G Category C to 150 kg. Heavier small unmanned aircraft (above 25 kg up to 150 kg) came under the Order. Passenger-carrying or still-heavier craft remain outside this ceiling. [source](https://www.info.gov.hk/gia/general/202507/17/P2025071700590.htm)
- 2025-10-27 — 1.4 GHz UAS (Private) Licence. A dedicated command-and-control band became available for Regulatory Sandbox projects. It is not a public mobile licence for anyone flying in Hong Kong. [source](https://www.ofca.gov.hk/en/industry_focus/industry_focus/uas_private_licence/index.html)
- 2025-11-24 — Regulatory Sandbox X. A second, harder trial programme started (traffic management, unconventional aircraft, possible cross-boundary tests). It is not “Sandbox phase 2 of the same 38 projects.” [source](https://www.info.gov.hk/gia/general/202511/24/P2025112400912.htm)
- 2025 (PA ¶153–157) — 2025 Policy Address ¶153–157. The government promised an Action Plan, Sandbox X, spectrum, and infrastructure language. The Action Plan document itself is still unpublished. [source](https://www.policyaddress.gov.hk/2025/en/p153.html)
- 2025-12-31 — Civil Aviation Department (CAD) Advisory Circular (AC)-013. Sets how to seek beyond-visual-line-of-sight permission inside the first Sandbox. It does not authorise BVLOS outside that sandbox. [source](https://www.cad.gov.hk/documents/AC-013_E.pdf)
- 2026-04-24 — CAD AC-017. Sets how to seek cross-boundary small unmanned aircraft permission inside Sandbox X. It does not mean a Shenzhen–Hong Kong route is already in commercial service. [source](https://www.cad.gov.hk/documents/AC-017.pdf)

## Mainland

These dates are Mainland law or drafts. They do not replace Cap. 448G in Hong Kong.

- 2023-12-21 — National Airspace Basic Classification. Mainland published G / W style labels. These are not Hong Kong airspace classes. [source](http://www.caac.gov.cn/XXGK/XXGK/TZTG/202312/t20231221_222397.html)
- 2024-01-01 — 国令761. These are the operating baseline for civil unmanned aircraft on the Mainland today. Cite them for Mainland ops, not for CAD permissions. [source](https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202306/content_6888800.htm)
- 2024-01-01 — CCAR-92. These are the operating baseline for civil unmanned aircraft on the Mainland today. Cite them for Mainland ops, not for CAD permissions. [source](https://xxgk.mot.gov.cn/2020/jigou/fgs/202401/t20240103_3980642.html)
- 2025-12-22 — NDRC LAE statistical classification. Defines how official statistics may count the low-altitude economy. It is not a Hong Kong value-added series and not a market forecast. [source](https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202512/content_7052866.htm)
- 2025-12-27 — Civil Aviation Law (2025 revision) — passage / promulgation. The revised law was passed, then took effect on 1 July 2026. Detailed unmanned-aircraft operating rules still sit in the 2024 instruments unless a new decree says otherwise. [source](https://www.caac.gov.cn/XXGK/XXGK/FLFG/202512/t20251227_229597.html)
- 2026-07-01 — Civil Aviation Law (2025 revision) — effective. The revised law was passed, then took effect on 1 July 2026. Detailed unmanned-aircraft operating rules still sit in the 2024 instruments unless a new decree says otherwise. [source](https://www.caac.gov.cn/XXGK/XXGK/FLFG/202512/t20251227_229597.html)
- 2026-08-11 — CAAC ATM Rules (征求意见稿) Ch.12 (draft). Consultation text only. Do not treat it as in-force traffic rules. [source](https://www.caac.gov.cn/HDJL/YJZJ/202608/t20260811_231462.html)

## United States

Early rows are studies and concepts. 2024–2025 rows are FAA rules for powered-lift pilots and operations. “Powered-lift” is the FAA category closest to many eVTOL designs.

- 2018-11-21 — NASA UAM Market Study. A sponsored study of constraints on urban air mobility demand. Use it for the constrained-versus-unconstrained idea; do not copy its dollar figures into a Hong Kong memo. [source](https://ntrs.nasa.gov/api/citations/20190001472/downloads/20190001472.pdf)
- 2021-01-15 — Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) Remote ID final rule (Federal Register (FR) publication). Published identification rules for unmanned aircraft in the US system. Hong Kong does not adopt this text by default. [source](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2021/01/15/2020-28948/remote-identification-of-unmanned-aircraft)
- 2023-04-26 — FAA UAM Concept of Operations v2.0. An operations concept, not a binding flight rule. [source](https://www.faa.gov/sites/faa.gov/files/Urban-Air-Mobility-Concept-of-Operations-2.0.pdf)
- 2024-11-21 — Integration of Powered-Lift final rule (89 FR 92296; Doc. 2024-24886). Creates pilot and operating rules for the powered-lift category (the closest FAA box to many eVTOL types). Effective date is not the same as type certification of a given aircraft. [source](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2024/11/21/2024-24886/integration-of-powered-lift-pilot-certification-and-operations-miscellaneous-amendments-related-to)
- 2025-01-21 — Powered-Lift final rule — general effective date. Creates pilot and operating rules for the powered-lift category (the closest FAA box to many eVTOL types). Effective date is not the same as type certification of a given aircraft. [source](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2024/11/21/2024-24886/integration-of-powered-lift-pilot-certification-and-operations-miscellaneous-amendments-related-to)
- 2025-07-24 — MOSAIC final rule (90 FR 35034; Doc. 2025-13972). Broadens light-sport certification paths; some pieces apply later (including 2026-07-24). Not a Hong Kong statute. [source](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2025/07/24/2025-13972/modernization-of-special-airworthiness-certification)
- 2025-10-22 — MOSAIC — first effective slice. Broadens light-sport certification paths; some pieces apply later (including 2026-07-24). Not a Hong Kong statute. [source](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2025/07/24/2025-13972/modernization-of-special-airworthiness-certification)
- 2026-07-24 — MOSAIC — deferred application / effective slice. Broadens light-sport certification paths; some pieces apply later (including 2026-07-24). Not a Hong Kong statute. [source](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2025/07/24/2025-13972/modernization-of-special-airworthiness-certification)

## European Union

2021–2023 created U-space (the EU traffic-management framework for drones). Later rows are EASA technical conditions for VTOL aircraft and crew, not a new U-space regulation.

- 2021-04-22 (adopted) / 2021-04-23 (OJ) — Implementing Regulation (EU) 2021/664 — U-space. Creates the U-space framework for drone traffic services in designated airspace. [source](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX%3A32021R0664)
- 2023-01-26 — (EU) 2021/664 application date. The framework applies from this day, but member states still have to designate U-space airspace. Application ≠ Union-wide dense U-space in every city. [source](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX%3A32021R0664)
- 2019-07-02 — European Union Aviation Safety Agency (EASA) SC-VTOL-01 (Issue 1). Airworthiness special condition for small VTOL-capable aircraft. It is how EASA certifies a type in the absence of a full CS-VTOL code. [source](https://www.easa.europa.eu/sites/default/files/dfu/SC-VTOL-01.pdf)
- 2025-07-07 — EASA ED Decision 2025/011/R. Adds crew and operations material for innovative air mobility / manned VTOL-capable aircraft. It is not a repeal of U-space. [source](https://www.easa.europa.eu/en/document-library/agency-decisions/ed-decision-2025011r)
